data.title: Consolidated Zarr metadata across L1+L2 corpus
data.summary: Run zarr.consolidate_metadata() once across the L1 and L2 corpora so every xarray.open_zarr() lands fast (~10ms) instead of falling back to a non-consolidated listing (10-100×slower). Eliminates the RuntimeWarning spam and removes a 0.5-2 s per-shot Zarr-open tax we saw on the failed signals job.

sections.body: Every ambix data audit / bulk-encode worker prints `RuntimeWarning: Failed to open Zarr store with consolidated metadata, but successfully read with non-consolidated metadata. This is typically much slower for opening a dataset.` On the 9,527-shot rbb corpus we already observed Zarr open dominating the per-shot wall time for the failed signals job (0% GPU util while CPU read the .zmetadata-less store). With 4 GPUs each fetching shots concurrently this becomes a real I/O bottleneck.

Run once across both corpora:

```python
import zarr
for shot_zarr in Path('/work/projects/imas_gpu/mast/level2/shots').glob('*.zarr'):
    zarr.consolidate_metadata(str(shot_zarr))
for shot_zarr in Path('/work/projects/imas_gpu/mast/level1/shots').glob('*.zarr'):
    zarr.consolidate_metadata(str(shot_zarr))
```

Writes a `.zmetadata` file at each shot root. Subsequent `open_zarr(..., consolidated=True)` reads it in one HTTP/GPFS roundtrip instead of recursively listing groups.

Measure `time xr.open_zarr(shot/rbb)` on three representative shots before/after:
  - shot 15085 (rbb era)
  - shot 28000 (mid corpus)
  - shot 30470 (most recent)
Target: ≥10× speed-up on open(). Confirm no RuntimeWarnings in the bulk-encode driver after.
Single-pass over the 11,573 L2 + ~17,111 L1 shots takes ~15 min on the login node (CPU only — pure metadata work, no array reads). Idempotent — safe to re-run when new shots arrive.

followups.title: Run zarr.consolidate_metadata() across L1 + L2 corpora
followups.body: Single CPU-only run. Idempotent. Should finish in ~15 min and eliminate the RuntimeWarning we see on every Zarr open. Sets the table for the 4-GPU bulk-encode to be GPU-bound rather than I/O-bound.
followups.est_turn: single Sonnet turn · ~30 min dev + ~15 min run
followups.prompt:
Project: imas-ambix
Plan: zarr-consolidate (§2)
Tier: sonnet

Context
  Every ambix data audit / bulk-encode emits a Zarr non-consolidated-metadata RuntimeWarning and pays a ~0.5-2 s per-shot open cost. Run zarr.consolidate_metadata() once across both corpora so subsequent opens are O(10 ms).

Done-when
  1. scripts/consolidate_zarr_metadata.py committed — single-file CLI, idempotent, takes --root and --workers.
  2. Run completes for both /work/projects/imas_gpu/mast/level1/shots/ and .../level2/shots/.
  3. /work/projects/imas_gpu/mast/level{1,2}/shots/<shot>.zarr/.zmetadata files exist for every shot.
  4. Validation: time `xr.open_zarr(...)` on 3 representative shots before/after, log to plan §3.
  5. data.impl → 1.0, status → shipped; followup resolved with the speed-up numbers.
